name: slotlock_list_resources
title: List calendar resources
description: List resources visible to the authenticated tenant principal, with what each says about itself: its name (show it rather than the reference), description, kind, capacity and labels, where it is (location), the groups it is in (a team, a department), and the pool it belongs to (a vehicle class, a room type). With kind, only resources of that kind; with labels, only those with every label given; with location, only those there or at a location in it; with group, only that group's. With pool, only that pool's members, in the order slotlock_book_pool tries them.

name: slotlock_get_free_busy
title: Get free-busy
description: When each resource is busy in a window, as busy intervals only (never whose or what), and whether that is certain (coverage: "uncertain" where a calendar feeding it has not been read lately). Name the resources with resource_ids, or select them instead by location (and every location in it), group, labels (every one), kind or pool: at most 100 (more answers selection_too_large, none selection_empty), named in selected_resource_ids.

name: slotlock_find_next_available
title: Find next available interval
description: Find the earliest certain interval that satisfies the requested duration (up to the 367-day search window, so a multi-month rental slot can be found). Name the resources with resource_ids, or select them as slotlock_get_free_busy does: at most 100.

name: slotlock_find_available_slots
title: Find available slots
description: List up to `limit` certain slots of the requested duration, earliest first across the resources, each one free of busy time and inside the resource's hours, to offer a person a choice. With require_free, only times when at least that many of the resources are free together, each slot naming them in resource_ids: every resource for a booking that needs them all (book it with slotlock_book_together), or any n of them. No slot is listed unless every resource's coverage is certain. Name the resources with resource_ids, or select them as slotlock_get_free_busy does: at most 20.

name: slotlock_find_available_ranges
title: Find available ranges
description: Find hires across days, such as a car from Friday to Monday: for each resource named, or each member of a pool, the earliest range that starts between pickup_start and pickup_end and either lasts `days` days (ending at the same local time) or ends between return_start and return_end. Each range is free throughout with its buffers, allowed by the resource's booking rules (pick-up and return times, lengths, notice, step) and starts and ends inside its bookable hours. Up to `limit` ranges, earliest first, one per resource; none unless every resource's coverage is certain. Book one with slotlock_create_event, or a pool's with slotlock_book_pool, at its start and end.

name: slotlock_create_event
title: Create resource event
description: Book a resource for a time, as an event of up to 3,660 days (a booking, lease or long rental). The database refuses a time already taken: 409 overlap, with alternatives (the earliest free times of the same length) and, when the booking in the way is yours, its id. A booking rule that refuses the time answers booking_rule_… with alternatives too. To book a time you hold, pass its hold_id, or use slotlock_confirm_slot. A retry with the same idempotency_key answers the same event.

dry_run.description: Check the write without making it: it runs with every check, the database's included, and is then undone, so nothing is stored, recorded or sent. The answer is what it would have been, with dry_run: true (ids in it are never stored), or the refusal it would have met, alternatives included. Charged as a read.
Present on a dry run only: nothing was stored.

name: slotlock_book_pool
title: Book from a pool
description: Book any one member of a pool (a vehicle class, a room type) for a time: members are tried in the pool's order (by id, fewest bookings in the last 30 days first, or in turn, as the tenant sets it) and the first that is free and allows the booking is booked, in one transaction, so a class sells out exactly at its number of members. The event names the member booked. 409 pool_full when none is free; 404 pool_not_found when the pool has no member you may book. A retry with the same idempotency_key answers the same event.

name: slotlock_get_pool_availability
title: Get pool availability
description: How many members of a pool (a vehicle class, a room type) are free across a window, each only where its booking rules let a booking start: the window split where that number changes, each part with how many are free, and coverage certainty. Book one with slotlock_book_pool. 404 pool_not_found when the pool has no member you may book.

name: slotlock_book_together
title: Book resources together
description: Book the same time on 2-20 resources at once, all or none: a van with its driver, a room with its projector. If any of them is taken, nothing is booked, and the refusal names that resource_id. Find such a time with slotlock_find_available_slots and require_free. A retry with the same idempotency_key answers the same events.

name: slotlock_get_event
title: Get resource event
description: Read one of your events by its id, with its revision (pass it as expected_revision to change or cancel it).

name: slotlock_list_events
title: List resource events
description: List your events that meet a time window, earliest first.

name: slotlock_update_event
title: Update resource event
description: Change one of your events at the revision you last read (expected_revision): its time, resource or details, all or nothing. A time already taken is 409 overlap with alternatives; a stale revision is 409 revision_conflict (read the event again). With expected_resource_id, the resource you read it on, an event since moved elsewhere is not found. To change only the time, slotlock_reschedule is simpler.

name: slotlock_delete_event
title: Delete resource event
description: Cancel one of your events at the revision you last read (expected_revision); a stale one is 409 revision_conflict. It cannot come back at that revision, so an old copy synced later does not restore it. slotlock_cancel does the same with fewer fields.

name: slotlock_hold_slots
title: Hold candidate slots
description: Hold up to five candidate slots for a short time (30-900 seconds) while a person chooses, as alternatives in one group: each free one is held, the others are listed with why not. Book one by passing its hold_id to slotlock_create_event, which releases the rest; unbooked holds expire on their own. A hold is yours alone, and you may have 20 live at once. A candidate refused for its time comes with alternatives (the earliest free times of its length). slotlock_confirm_slot books a held time.

A retry answers the same event (replayed).
